title: `x + 0.0` and `0.0 - x` keep or flip a zero's sign
verdict: `zero_sign`: not IEEE either, so up to one zero (`canon`)
description: `-0.0 + 0.0` is `-0.0` and `0.0 - 0.0` (as `0.0 - x`) is `-0.0`, where IEEE 754 gives `+0.0` for both under round-to-nearest; `-0.0 - 0.0` is `-0.0`, as IEEE gives. The sign of a zero result of `+` and `-` is therefore Polars's own (polars-zero-sign).

The same finding as polars-zero-sign-streaming (which supersedes polars-zero-sign): the literal shortcuts `x + 0.0 → x` and `0.0 - x → -x` run on both engines once a morsel holds more than one row; on streaming frames under about 100 rows (one-row morsels) the IEEE zero comes back (`s-zero-sign-literal`). This fact keeps its id for the engine tables that cite it.
reference: One zero (`zero_sign: ONE_ZERO`, #89): `-0.0` is `0.0` everywhere, so the translation canonicalises (`one_zero`) where a result's zeros are observed.
